utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, for once the Prosecution agrees with you when it says that if your telephone lines are being tapped, this may have an impact on the fairness of the trial. This is the Prosecutor's position. The best thing to do would be to appoint a counsel for you. This is what the Prosecution is saying. Second point. What I'm telling you is this: I don't have all the information relating to this matter. The Registrar did not discuss this with the Chamber, did not inform the Chamber about it, and took this decision without consulting us. It seems that the Registry had information coming from your former right-hand man and things mentioned with the major, that when you were on the phone with him, you discussed political matters. In light of this, the Registry felt that this telephone line was provided to you by this Tribunal to prepare your Defence and not to discuss any other matters. And as far as I'm concerned, this is what led to the Registrar's decision. But there is not only that ground, there's another ground which I had rather not address, which is connected to the witness. The fact that your conversations are being tapped just means, from the Registrar's standpoint, that you do not use this telephone line for reasons other than your Defence. If, for instance, you phone up Mr. Krasic to tell him that he needs to work on such-and-such a witness's testimony, then this is part of your Defence, and that is not a problem. But if you tell Mr. Krasic that during the parliamentary assembly, a bill will have to be amended, then you are no longer talking about the same thing, and I'm sure you understand what I mean. As I see things, I don't know what the Prosecutor is going to do, but I think there are going to be new motions filed, new applications, new Appeals Chamber decisions. The trial was making progress. We've heard 40 witnesses so far, and the Prosecution needs 10 or so hours to finish its case. Mr. Seselj, we have five minutes left before we finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to add something as regards the decision taken by the Registrar. We were advised of the fact that the Registrar sent a letter to Mr. Seselj's associates, asking them to provide further explanation. They responded to the letter, but did not respond to the questions, and that is why the Registrar took its decision. This is what we were advised of. This was no arbitrary decision taken by the Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to tell you one thing briefly here at this point. David Tolbert was for years the deputy secretary of Hans Holthuis, so deputy Registrar; and in that capacity, every month over a seven-month period he -- and this was in 2004, he prohibited me from having any contacts at all with my family, with my friends, with everybody, both telephones and visits. So for seven months, I was in a state of absolute isolation. One of the explanations given was that my party, the Serbian Radical Party, had achieved a very good result at the parliamentary elections, and so there was the danger of me influencing the establishment of the formation of a new government which wasn't in the interests of peace, and this Tribunal was set up to promote peace in the Balkans. And after a certain amount of time, this same man, David Tolbert, left the Registry and became the Deputy Chief Prosecutor, Carla Del Ponte's Deputy Chief Prosecutor, and there you have a flagrant example of this feedback relationship, a very strong one, between the Secretariat and the OTP, Prosecution. And now to have me allow the Registry to intercept my communications and listen in, I'm not going to do that. Even if they do, they're not allowed to use that if they do it clandestinely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can perfectly well state all of this and challenge this decision and submit it to the President of the Tribunal. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Two very quick points. I'm aware of the time. First of all, I want to make it absolutely clear that when I spoke earlier about the fairness issues with respect to the trial, I was referring to the abuse of the privilege by the accused as found by the Registrar and not necessarily the monitoring of his communications that goes to the issue of fairness, and that relates to fairness from the Prosecution perspective. Secondly, in light of the fact that the Registrar's decision or letter to the accused is apparently not a public document, I do want to put on the record part of what was contained in the Registry's statement announcing this to the press, in which it was found, quoting from the Registrar's letter, that there were reasonable grounds, and I'm quoting: " ... reasonable grounds to believe that the privilege is being abused in an attempt to interfere with or intimidate witnesses or interfere with the administration of justice." Those are the publicly-stated grounds that Mr. Holthuis relied upon in making the determination that the privileged communications would cease, and I think it's important that that is it not necessarily relate to any political activities of the accused, at least with respect to what's in the public domain that's contained in this letter. And so his findings are based on reasonable grounds to believe that there's attempts at interference or intimidation of witnesses and/or interference with the administration of justice, and those are the publicly-stated reasons why this privileged communications has been temporarily withdrawn or suspended by the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Simply, to make sure that everything is clear, I had not heard of any press release which refers to one of the rules of our Rules which entitles communications to be regulated, when there is interference or intimidation of witnesses. I have a personal question. How does the Registry know that there is a case of intimidation of witnesses? That said, it is now time to stop. Mr. Mundis, you would like to add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: VWS is part of the Registry, of course, so in light of the fact that the Registrar controls VWS, there very well may have been independent sources of information from VWS going to the Registry that supported the Registrar's decision; so that would seem to be the source of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We want everything to be quite clear on the transcript. To date, the Trial Chamber has not been seized of any report filed by the VWS as regards witness intimidation; never, ever. If such a report is in support of the Registrar's letter, it would have been important for us to see this, but we have never seen any such thing. We shall resume next week, and I believe we are sitting in the morning. We shall resume on Tuesday at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of October, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.56 p.m.,
